newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Turkey increasing security cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Turkey increasing security cooperation.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held talks with Turkish Defence Minister Turhan Tayan on Friday as part of increasing defence cooperation.
"Our meeting represents the tightening cooperation between Israel and Turkey in all realms and foremost in the security realm," Netanyahu was quoted by his office as saying.

Tayan arrived on Wednesday in a further blow to the presitge of Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, who won elections 16 months ago partly on a promise to cut military ties to the Jewish state.
Tayan, from the secularist wing of Erbakan's coalition government, was due to return to Turkey later on Friday.

"There is room for additional cooperation primarily in the economic and security realm, such as the fight against terrorism and the preservation of stability in the region," Netanyahu was quoted as saying at the start of his talks with Tayan.
Turkey and Israel have signed defence cooperation pacts which drew an angry response from Iran and many in the Arab world. Israeli planes have flown training flights in Turkey under the accords.
While in Israel, Tayan met Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai and visited Israel Aircraft Industries, which is modernising Turkey's F-4 jet fighters.
